\[
n\lambda = 2d \sin\theta
\]

The maximum wavelength occurs when \(\sin\theta = 1\), so the equation simplifies to:

\[
\lambda_{\text{max}} = \frac{2d}{n}
\]

Here, \(n = 2\) (second-order diffraction). For platinum, which has a face-centered cubic (FCC) structure, the interplanar spacing \(d\) for the (100) planes is equal to the lattice parameter \(a\). The lattice parameter of platinum is approximately \(a = 2.88 \, \text{Å} = 2.88 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{m}\).

Substituting \(d = a = 2.88 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{m}\) and \(n = 2\) into the equation:

\[
\lambda_{\text{max}} = \frac{2 \cdot (2.88 \times 10^{-10})}{2} = 2.88 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{m}
\]

Thus, the maximum wavelength is:

\[
\boxed{2.88 \times 10^{-10}}
\]"]

   \[
   V = 13.056 \, \text{V}

\]
